Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
In the worst case, a single vertex can have outgoing edges to every other vertex in the directed graph, making the maximum cost for one operation equal to |V| - 1.

Using aggregate analysis, the total cost across all |V| operations is simply the sum of outgoing edges from each vertex, which equals the total number of edges |E| in the graph. Therefore, the average amortized cost per operation is |E| / |V|.

* The worst possible single operation has cost |V| - 1, which occurs when a vertex has outgoing edges to all other vertices in the graph.
* The average amortized cost based on aggregate analysis is |E| / |V|, since the sum of all operation costs equals the total edge count |E| divided by the |V| total operations.
